description: REGRESSION WALL for saga #811, flipped by issue #815 from the characterization issue #816 built against the broken build. It asserts the CORRECT behaviour now: the check before execution runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 over the whole program and, on an `error`-severity finding, **Phase 2 never begins** — "no instruction executes, no trace event is emitted" (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`). So the `events` array is EMPTY, and that emptiness is the assertion: before the fix this program ran, produced events, and reported nothing, which is the silent wrong answer the saga is named for. Reverting the gate turns this red. Fault shape B — a KNOWN command used in VALUE position (issue #716, re-parented under saga #811). This is a DIFFERENT fault from shape A and the fixtures record it separately on purpose, and the distinction was load-bearing: `check()` was CLEAN here, not merely unconsulted — `forward` resolves fine once `turtle-rendering` is active — so saga #811's stated mechanism ("`check()` computes the right answer and `execute()` never consults it") was true of shape A only. Shape B therefore needed a new checker rule rather than only the gate, which is why #815 reports it uniformly across every form rather than per-form — the inconsistency #716 recorded. Form under test: `right <command>` — one turtle command consuming another as its angle. Its `-check` sibling reports the identical finding.
